findings.title: WRAP step dictates `np.mod` with no guard, which can break SC7's half-open range
findings.description:
Task 2.2 tells the implementer to use `np.mod(positions[:, 0], width, out=...)` and says it produces values "in `[0, width)`". In floating point that is not always true. For a tiny negative overshoot, such as `-1e-17` or `np.nextafter(0, -1)`, `np.mod(x, 100.0)` returns exactly `100.0`, because `x + 100` rounds to `100`. That position falls outside `[0, width)` and breaks SC7 ("maps every agent position into the half-open rectangle… in a single call"). The current `src/migratory_server/bounds_enforcement.py:59-60` matches the dictated code and has no guard. The test list in Task 2.3 has no case for it. Only exact multiples like `(100, 50)` are tested, and those work. The integration assertion `0 <= x < width` in Task 3.4 could therefore fail at random.

Fix:
- Add a step after the `np.mod` that sets any value `>= width` (or `>= height`) to `0.0`.
- Add a test `test_wrap_tiny_negative_overshoot` using `np.nextafter(0.0, -1.0)`.

findings.title: Config-defaults change is committed before any test run
findings.description:
Section 4 changes `config/test.yaml` and `config/default.yaml` from OPEN to WRAP behavior. Any existing test that loads `config/test.yaml` and checks positions or motion could change behavior. Tasks 4.1 and 4.2 only check that the file loads with `python -c`. Task 4.3 then commits. The first full `pytest` after this change is Task 5.1, which comes after the commit, so commit 4.3 is not at a tested point.

Fix: add a `pytest` run to Section 4 before the commit marker. Task 5.1 can then be dropped (see the proportionality note).

findings.title: Commit markers are checkbox items inside standalone "Commit" tasks
findings.description:
Tasks 1.5, 2.4, 3.6, 4.3 and 5.5 are each a whole task made of checkbox items (`- [ ] git add …`, `- [ ] **Commit:** …`). Commit markers should be plain `**Commit**:` lines, never checkboxes. With checkboxes, the task-checker has to tick commit steps, and a later "checks-only" commit tends to follow, which project rules forbid.

Fix: replace each commit task with one plain line, e.g. `**Commit**: feat: add BoundsPolicy enum and WorldBoundsConfig.policy field`, placed at the end of the task that precedes it. The markers are otherwise at sensible points, one per working section.

findings.title: SC2 dataclass default is not tested directly
findings.description: Task 1.3 has the loader resolve a missing key to `OPEN` explicitly. So `test_bounds_policy_omitted_defaults_open` passes even if the dataclass field had no default. SC2 says `WorldBoundsConfig` itself defaults to `OPEN`, and Task 1.2's success criterion says the same, but no test checks it. Adding one assertion `WorldBoundsConfig(width=1.0, height=1.0).policy is BoundsPolicy.OPEN` to Task 1.4 would cover it.

findings.title: Round-trip test is weaker than SC5
findings.description: SC5 says "reloading the emitted YAML produces an equal `ServerConfig`". Task 1.4's test only checks that `policy` matches. Since `ServerConfig` is a frozen dataclass, the test can compare the whole reloaded object with `==` at no extra cost. Serialization itself is fine: `config_to_yaml` already passes values through `_serialize_for_yaml`, which turns StrEnum values into plain strings (`src/migratory_server/config.py:663-681`).

findings.title: Proportionality: redundant runs and tests to trim
findings.description:
For a 2/5-effort slice, a few items repeat each other:
- Full `pytest` runs three times: Task 3.5, Task 5.1, and Task 5.2 Step 2. Once the Section 4 run is added, Task 5.1 can go.
- The parametrized "dispatches correctly and does not raise" test at line 171 duplicates the per-policy tests. Cut it.
- `test_open_is_noop_positions` and `test_open_is_noop_velocities` can be one test.
- `test_reflect_clamps_top_edge` and `test_reflect_clamps_bottom_edge` could be parametrized together with the left and right edge tests.

None of this is blocking.

findings.title: Walkthrough Step 8 leaves `test.yaml` policy open, though SC12 requires `wrap`
findings.description: "Restore `config/test.yaml` to whichever policy you want to keep (recommend `wrap`)" invites leaving `reflect` or `open` in place. That would break SC12, and Task 5.5's `git add` list does not include config files. Change the step to: restore `policy: wrap` and confirm `git diff config/` is empty.

findings.title: Task 3.2 asks to confirm "zero import-time overhead" while adding a top-level import
findings.description: The same task adds a module-level `from migratory_server.bounds_enforcement import apply_bounds_policy`. The Notes at line 329 admit the import is not avoided. A junior implementer may stall on this contradiction. Reword to "no function call or array slicing on the OPEN path."

findings.title: Frontmatter says `status: complete` while every box is unchecked
findings.description: Task 5.3 is the step meant to set this status. Until then the file should read `status: not-started` (or `in-progress`).
